resumen: Adverbios negativos al inicio (never, rarely, seldom, little, under no circumstances): el auxiliar va antes del sujeto, como en una pregunta: Never have I seen…, Little did we know…
Hardly … when / No sooner … than, con past perfect: Hardly had we left when it rained., No sooner had I sat down than the phone rang.
Not only … but also: la inversión va solo en la primera parte: Not only was he late, but he also forgot the tickets.
Not until / Only then: la inversión va en la cláusula principal: Not until I got home did I realise…, Only then did she understand.
Condicionales invertidos (formales, sin if): Had I known…, Were I to win…, Should you need anything…
So + adjetivo al inicio también invierte: So loud was the music that nobody could hear.
Oraciones hendidas para destacar un elemento: It was Marco who broke it., What I need is a holiday.
Do enfático (do/does/did + infinitivo) para insistir o contradecir: I did send it! = sí que lo envié.

preguntas.q: I know you think I forgot, but I ___ send you the email yesterday; check your spam folder.
preguntas.x: El do enfático (do/does/did + infinitivo sin to) refuerza una afirmación que alguien duda: I did send it = «sí que lo envié». Con yesterday hace falta did; have send y was send no son formas posibles.

preguntas.q: I didn't break the printer! It was Marco ___ broke it.
preguntas.x: En las oraciones hendidas It was + persona + who… se destaca quién hizo algo; who (o that) es el sujeto de broke. Whom solo funciona como objeto y which no se usa para personas.

preguntas.q: I don't need more advice. ___ is a long holiday somewhere quiet.
preguntas.x: Las oraciones hendidas con what destacan una información: What I need is a holiday (= «lo que necesito es…»). What ya significa «lo que», por eso no se dice the thing what ni se empieza con That o Which.

preguntas.a: Seldom have I met such a talented young programmer.
d: Never I have seen such a beautiful sunset.
Rarely we eat out during the week.
Never did I saw anything like it.
preguntas.x: Never, rarely y seldom al inicio de la oración exigen inversión con auxiliar: Seldom have I met…, Rarely do we eat out…. Tras el auxiliar invertido, el verbo va en su forma normal: did I see, no did I saw.

preguntas.q: Not only ___ late, but he also forgot the tickets.
preguntas.x: Con Not only al inicio hay inversión en la primera parte: Not only was he late, but he also…. Con el verbo be se invierte el propio was; did solo aparece con otros verbos (Not only did he forget…).

preguntas.q: Hardly ___ the house when it started to pour with rain.
preguntas.x: Hardly … when (= «apenas … cuando») va con past perfect invertido: Hardly had we left when…. Sin inversión (Hardly we had left) es incorrecto en esta posición, y el present perfect no encaja en un relato en pasado.

preguntas.q: No sooner ___ sat down ___ the phone rang.
preguntas.x: No sooner lleva inversión (had I sat) y se completa con than, porque es una comparación: No sooner had I sat down than the phone rang (= «en cuanto me senté, sonó el teléfono»). Then es «entonces» y no sirve aquí.

preguntas.q: Under no circumstances ___ your password with anyone, not even IT staff.
preguntas.x: Under no circumstances (= «bajo ningún concepto») es una expresión negativa y exige inversión: should you share. Añadir not (shouldn't you share) crearía una doble negación.

preguntas.a: Little did we know that the company was about to close.
d: Only then she realised how serious the problem was.
Under no circumstances you should leave the door open.
Not only he forgot the tickets, but he was also late.
preguntas.x: Little al inicio (= «qué poco sabíamos») exige inversión con auxiliar: Little did we know…. Las otras tres necesitan lo mismo: Only then did she realise, Under no circumstances should you leave, Not only did he forget.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “I didn't realise I'd lost my keys until I got home.”
preguntas.a: Not until I got home did I realise I'd lost my keys.
d: Not until I got home I realised I'd lost my keys.
Not until did I get home I realised I'd lost my keys.
Until I got home did I realise I'd lost my keys.
preguntas.x: Con Not until + momento o cláusula al inicio, la inversión va en la cláusula principal: Not until I got home did I realise…. La cláusula de until no se invierte, y sin not no hay inversión posible.

preguntas.q: ___ about the train strike, I would have taken a taxi.
preguntas.x: En el tercer condicional se puede suprimir if e invertir had: Had I known = If I had known. No se mezclan if e inversión (If had I known), y esta inversión solo es posible con had, were y should.

preguntas.q: ___ any further information, please do not hesitate to contact me.
preguntas.x: Should you need… es un condicional invertido y formal (= If you need…), muy típico de los correos profesionales. Solo should funciona así: would y shall no, y no se combina if con la inversión.

preguntas.q: ___ the lottery, I would give half of it to charity.
preguntas.x: Were I to + infinitivo es la versión invertida y formal de If I were to win (segundo condicional, algo improbable). En la inversión solo vale were, nunca was, y would no va en la parte de la condición.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “The music was so loud that nobody could hear the speaker.”
preguntas.a: So loud was the music that nobody could hear the speaker.
d: So loud the music was that nobody could hear the speaker.
So the music was loud that nobody could hear the speaker.
Such loud was the music that nobody could hear the speaker.
preguntas.x: Para dar énfasis, so + adjetivo pasa al inicio y el verbo se invierte: So loud was the music that…. Such va con un sustantivo (such loud music), no con un adjetivo solo.
